correctness.rationale: The reduction from arbitrary translations to centered rectangles is exact by convexity and central symmetry. Equal-length diagonals encode every rectangle. At any optimizer one diagonal vertex lies on the rhombus boundary; an interior equal-length partner must be perpendicular by angular first variation. Orthogonal pairs are bounded using endpoint minima of a strictly concave trigonometric denominator and AM-GM. Boundary pairs are classified exactly by equal values of one quadratic and sharp endpoint bounds. Both constructions attain the respective sharp values, and equality constraints plus supporting sides exclude other optima or translations. The standalone finite verifier returned VERIFY_OK; it is diagnostic, not an exhaustive proof.

value.rationale: Unrestricted maximum-area inscribed rectangles are a motivated canonical convex geometry problem (Cabello et al. 2014). This computes an entire natural one-parameter family with a genuine sharp bifurcation between non-square side-midpoint and vertex-anchored square optima, including the exactly two optimizer coexistence point and uniqueness elsewhere. The distinct geometric mechanisms are not captured by the universal half-area existence theorem, axis-parallel textbook computation, or the square case alone. The result is a complete geometric classification, not a renaming or arbitrary finite table.
